Re-validated every carried figure in the dispatch description against live files and confirmed all of them, including by direct invocation: the deployed sapience-remember.sh --dry-run already exits 0 with provenance '[repo:nvim] ...', token redacted and explicit:true, so deliverable (d) is a pure test-coverage gap. user_decision.question: settings-fragment.json still grants all four MCP write tools at this repo's project scope, including two the extension's own text says never to use. Keeping the grant leaves a stray proactive MCP call able to succeed non-interactively and land a permanent, undeletable untagged write; narrowing it adds a mechanical second line of defense but leaves core/context/patterns/mcp-server-ownership.md's worked example (which cites the current four-tool grant by path) stale, and core/ is outside this task's declared edit target.
options: Keep the four-tool grant intact; record the residual and its promotion criterion in the new write-path rule (this plan's route)
Narrow the grant now by dropping sapience_remember and sapience_wrapup from the allow-list, accepting that mcp-server-ownership.md's worked example goes stale until a follow-up task fixes it
Keep the grant here and file a separate follow-up task that narrows it together with the core/ worked-example update, so neither surface is left inconsistent
user_decision.recommended: Keep the four-tool grant intact; record the residual and its promotion criterion in the new write-path rule (this plan's route)
user_decision.obligation: Deliverable (b) and acceptance criterion 3: the standing rule must exist with its advisory-or-enforced status recorded. The recommended route discharges this with an advisory, path-scoped rules/sapience-write-path.md whose own text records the kept-grant residual, the rejected-mechanization rationale, and the promotion criterion that would justify enforcement -- checkable by reading that file after Phase 4.
